title: Last-coordinate splitting of the functional
statement: Let $n,m\ge0$, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, and let $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. If $f_0,f_1$ and $g_{j,0},g_{j,1}$ denote their restrictions to the last coordinate and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, then $F_P(f,(g_j)_j)$ equals $\bigl(F_P(f_0,(d_f,g_{j,0})_j)+F_P(f_1,(d_f,g_{j,1})_j)\bigr)/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is an $m$-tuple of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. Let $f$ be a real function and $g$ a vector of $m$ real functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $g_b(x)=g(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_g,d_g$ componentwise. Then $F_P(f,g)=\bigl(F_P(f_0,(d_f,g_0))+F_P(f_1,(d_f,g_1))\bigr)/2$, where $(d_f,g_b)$ adjoins $d_f$ to the additional coordinates.
